text: The Patriots face the Steelers in Week 2 dealing with some notable roster upheaval: Carlton Davis III is officially out at cornerback, forcing the defense to shuffle its secondary against Pittsburgh's offense, though the Steelers themselves will be without starting receiver Michael Pittman Jr. On the brighter side, RB TreVeyon Henderson—who sat out the opener with an ankle injury—declared himself "ready to go" and is expected to return to action, while the team elevated P Mitch Wishnowsky from the practice squad for the second consecutive week. Off the field, the Patriots honored an institution this week when Stephon Gilmore, the 2019 NFL Defensive Player of the Year and two-time All-Pro cornerback who defined an era of New England defense, signed a one-day contract to retire as a member of the Patriots, cementing his legacy as one of the greatest corners in franchise history. Meanwhile, Patriots owner Robert Kraft made headlines for a different reason, announcing that he had Macklemore removed as an opening act for Ed Sheeran's upcoming shows at Gillette Stadium over what Kraft described as "a history of antisemitic rhetoric and imagery that we believe has been deeply offensive and hurtful to the Jewish community."
